column3: Mode-selection reference: interactive/print/JSON/RPC table, exit-code contract per mode, RpcClient guidance, and the piConfig rebrand keys.
Complete CLI reference: modes, --model/--thinking, session flags and their mutual exclusions, the +name/-name tool delta syntax, resource flags, package/credential/MCP subcommands.
Spec for the codemode tool: QuickJS script sandbox, tools.* calling, text/image/console output, store/load, models.classify/generateImages, and the hard limits (256MB VM, 2 workers, 16MiB output).

Densest mechanism doc: compaction and branch summarization triggers, cut-point rules, split user-message spans, CompactionEntry/BranchSummaryEntry shapes, the summary format, and the session_before_compact/session_compact_failed/session_before_tree hooks.
File-location contract for the agent directory, the project .pi directory, and context files; notes that only sessionDir is read before trust resolution.
Four isolation methods (plain Docker, Docker Sandboxes, OpenShell, Gondolin) with an honest table of what each actually protects, including the Gondolin env-inheritance caveat.
Provider-extension guide: registration forms, auth syntax, the six-step custom streamSimple contract, the onPayload/onResponse/onProviderStreamEvent hooks, and a provider test checklist.
Docs-site navigation config: three navigation groups, a nested Reference group, and four legacy redirects.
Three uses of env vars: process markers, the shell-tool session environment (PI_SESSION_ID/PROVIDER/MODEL/REASONING_LEVEL), and the Pi process configuration table.
The extension reference: lifecycle events, the handler-composition table, tool definition and exposure tiers, nested tool calls, state storage, MCP registration, and mode/UI behaviour.
49-line normative summary of the agent loop, the entry tree, context assembly, sessions, interfaces and the extension/skill/resource model.

Binary PNG (1600x1442) screenshot of the DOOM overlay running inside Pi; opened via the image reader to confirm it shows the game composited over the live transcript with Pi's status footer beneath, but pixel data is not line-by-line readable.

Binary PNG (1025x847) illustration in docs/images that no page in this shard references; opened via the image reader to confirm it is an antique engraved woodcut of a porcupinefish on a transparent background, but pixel data is not line-by-line readable.

Binary PNG (1500x1736) screenshot of the interactive TUI; opened via the image reader to confirm it shows the startup header with the [Context]/[Skills]/[Prompts]/[Extensions]/[Themes] resource listing and the token/cost/model footer, but pixel data is not line-by-line readable.

Binary PNG (1720x1116) screenshot of the session tree view; opened via the image reader to confirm it shows a flattened branch with per-tool-call rows and an (aborted) assistant turn, but pixel data is not line-by-line readable.
Landing page: the four CLI integration modes, the resource-mechanism chooser table, and the first-screen statement that project trust does not sandbox tool calls.
Canonical event reference shared by JSON and RPC mode, with the delta-only message_update rule and the reconstruction contract (replace with text_end/toolcall_end/message_end).
Every named keybinding action and default, per-platform overrides, and the keybindings.json format.
llama.cpp router setup, /llama model management, and the chat-model-as-classifier next-token technique with its context and accuracy caveats.

MCP reference: server config and merge rules, connection lifecycle and wait policy, OAuth, the exposure/toolExposure model, resources, and the statement that every MCP call passes the extension tool_call/tool_result gates.
The AgentMessage union and every content block, including the section-patching SystemMessage, the stopReason set, the nestedCalls record, and the four coding-agent roles.

Generated field reference for models.json: provider/model/modelOverrides fields, input limits, pricing tiers, and ~40 named per-API compatibility flags including session-affinity and mid-conversation system-message support.

Model selection and configuration: credential precedence, compatible endpoints, image resize and prompt-cache lifetimes, samplingParamsByThinkingLevel merge order, and the classifier/image model families.
Converts an NVIDIA single-model llama.cpp recipe into a router preset, with the exact flag-to-preset-key mapping, the load-on-startup rule and the note that the build must advertise --models-preset.

Package distribution contract: conventional directories vs the pi manifest, resource filters, the rule against listing host-provided packages in dependencies, and the package identity rules that prevent double loading.

Prompt-template contract: frontmatter description and argument-hint, the six argument substitution forms, shell-like quoting, and the fact that extensions see the raw input first through the input event.

Provider authentication reference: /login and /logout, the full environment-variable table, the !command key syntax, per-provider env objects, and the OpenRouter/Azure/Bedrock/Cloudflare/Vertex specifics.
Install-and-first-task walkthrough plus the "choose how to customize Pi" ladder ordered by increasing power.

Every RPC stdin command with payload and response shape: prompt/steer/follow_up with mandatory streamingBehavior, abort/clear_queue, model and thinking commands, compact, retry, bash with excludeFromContext, session commands, get_entries with a durable since cursor, and get_tree.
The extension-UI subprotocol: blocking dialog methods vs fire-and-forget methods, the explicit degraded list outside TUI mode, and the request/response record shapes.
RPC process protocol: record families, id correlation, the LF-only framing rule (readline breaks on U+2028/U+2029), the prompt disposition semantics, error shapes and shutdown.
In-process SDK reference: the five substitutable services, SessionManager authority over context, steer/followUp must be explicit, event subscription, and the built-in extension factories.
Security posture: project trust as a resource-loading gate rather than a sandbox, the trust decision order, the sessionDir exception, and the four isolation options.
Persisted JSONL contract: every entry type, the section-patching system message, the append-only context_edit, the three-stage context build (entries/projection/messages) and version migration.
User-facing session workflow: the /tree vs /fork vs /clone intent table, compaction behaviour, storage location, and the export/share credential warning.

Every user setting with type, default and purpose, including the +name/-name defaultTools delta, codemode.mode/inlineBudget, compaction and branchSummary groups, and the rule to keep retry.provider.maxRetries at 0.
Which shell Pi uses, the shellPath/shellCommandPrefix settings, and the shopt -s expand_aliases recipe for Bash aliases.
Skill mechanism: SKILL.md directory form, name+description-only system-prompt advertising, the description-as-trigger rule, frontmatter fields, and the /skill:name manual escape hatch.
The built-in slash-command list in four groups, plus the note that built-in TUI commands are excluded from get_commands.
Per-terminal configuration for modified keys, IME, images and colours, plus the OSC 7501 program-status protocol (working/blocked/done/error/idle) that never carries content.
Termux/Android setup: shared storage, clipboard via termux-clipboard-set/get, and the AGENTS.md block to write for an Android environment.
Theme format (vars/colors/export, six colour notations), the system theme's contrast rules and 100ms query budget, and the strict-object validation.
Enabling extended keys in tmux (CSI-u for 3.5+, modifyOtherKeys for 3.2-3.4) so Shift+Enter and Alt+Enter survive the multiplexer.
Terminal component reference: integration points, visible-width measurement, Focusable/CURSOR_MARKER and IME focus propagation, overlays, theming tokens, and render-cache discipline.
Interactive-mode walkthrough: Enter vs Alt+Enter delivery semantics, ! vs !! commands, /tree /fork /clone, and the /debug log warning.

Virtual-model reference: selection vs dispatch kept in separate records, route() request fields and reason values (user/continuation/retry/direct), branch-following router state, and cache-preservation rules.
Native Windows vs WSL: the Bash and PowerShell resolution orders, the optional powershell tool flags, and WSL path-conversion limits.
Examples index: one paragraph per directory, the note that the examples are typechecked with the repo, and the instruction to build dist/cli.js first.

214-line catalogue of every extension example grouped by intent, plus the two taught patterns: StringEnum for string parameters (Google-API compatibility) and state persistence in tool-result details.
Commits on session_shutdown using the last assistant message's first line as the message; uses pi.exec and getEntries, prefixes the message with [pi].
30-line example of createBashTool's spawnHook rewriting command/cwd/env before every bash call; re-registers the tool with a wrapped execute.
/bookmark and /unbookmark commands calling pi.setLabel on the last assistant entry, with a generated default label from Date.now().
Custom editor that replaces its first/last rendered line with a fitted border carrying a spinner, model, thinking level, context usage, cwd and git branch; fitBorder truncates the right label first.
Re-registers read/bash/edit/write with the original definitions spread in and only renderCall/renderResult replaced, demonstrating that behaviour and presentation are separable.
Scans .claude/rules/*.md at session_start and appends a "## Project Rules" list of paths to the system prompt so the model reads them on demand.
/commands command listing pi.getCommands() grouped by source, with argument completion for extension/prompt/skill and a follow-up that reveals a command's source path.
Confirms before session_before_switch (new vs resume, checking for user messages) and session_before_fork; returns {cancel:true} to refuse.
Replaces the compaction summary with a full-context summary from a cheaper model (gemini-2.5-flash); reuses preparation.firstKeptEntryId and falls back to the default on error or empty summary.
Custom footer component showing token/cost totals, model and git branch; returns a dispose hook that unsubscribes from footerData.onBranchChange.
Replaces the startup header with a block-character ASCII mascot and a version subtitle; restoring is done with ctx.ui.setHeader(undefined).
Single line node_modules/ so the example's own dependency root stays out of git.
Custom provider with PKCE OAuth login, token refresh and a hand-written streamSimple; first 130 of 617 lines read (OAuth and stream plumbing beyond that not read line by line).

Generated npm lockfile (24 lines, one dependency: @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.52.0 with integrity hash); machine-generated, nothing to read line by line - the only non-obvious fact is that its root package name (pi-extension-custom-provider) differs from package.json.
Manifest making the directory a loadable Pi extension (pi.extensions: ./index.ts) with @anthropic-ai/sdk as its own dependency; scripts are deliberate no-ops.
Single line node_modules/ for the GitLab Duo example's dependency root.
Provider delegating to pi-ai's built-in anthropicMessagesApi/openAIResponsesApi behind the GitLab AI gateway, with an exported MODELS table for the test script; first 130 of 405 lines read.
Manifest with pi.extensions and no dependencies, proving an extension can be written entirely against host-provided packages.
Standalone provider harness: reads credentials from auth.json, registers the API, streams a one-shot prompt and prints each event type; the only test-like file in the shard.
Opt-in raw provider-stream viewer: buffers provider_stream_event per assistant message, structuredClones the payloads and persists them as an expandable debug-provider-events custom entry.
Blocks session switches and forks while git status is dirty, counting changed files and failing closed when there is no UI.
Two lines: a comment and doom1.wad, keeping the runtime-downloaded shareware WAD out of git.
DOOM overlay guide: usage, the control table, the half-block (U+2588) 24-bit rendering trick and the 3.2:1 aspect correction; its quoted overlay sizes disagree with index.ts.
Renders DOOM frames as half-block characters with 24-bit colour, converts ARGB to RGBA, ticks at 35 FPS and treats a WASM throw as a quit.
WebAssembly wrapper: evals doom.js via new Function to bypass jiti, injects the WAD into the Emscripten FS, builds argv in the WASM heap and exposes tick/getFrameRGBA/pushKey.
DOOM keycode table plus the terminal-to-DOOM mapping, accepting both raw characters and Kitty-protocol sequences and pushing two codes for shifted keys.
Emscripten build script: clones doomgeneric, copies the platform file, and lists ~90 C sources plus the exact exported functions and MODULARIZE/EXPORT_NAME flags.

Generated minified Emscripten glue module (64KB in 21 lines, one ~62KB statement); first 12 lines read to confirm the createDoomModule factory, but machine-generated minified output is not readable line by line and its behaviour is fixed by the emcc flags in doom/build.sh.

Binary WebAssembly module (380KB); first 16 bytes hex-dumped and confirmed to carry the 0061736d 01000000 WASM magic/version, but a compiled binary has no textual structure - its exported surface is enumerated in doom/build.sh and typed in doom-engine.ts.
72-line doomgeneric platform shim exposing the framebuffer pointer and a 256-entry key ring buffer to JS via EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE, with no sound and no-op timing.
/doom-overlay command: ensures a WAD, reuses or creates a module-level DoomEngine (so a second run resumes) and opens ctx.ui.custom with centred overlay options.
Locates the WAD in the bundle or default paths, or downloads the shareware WAD, gunzips it and verifies the IWAD magic before writing it.
Eight-line example skill with only name and description frontmatter, proving a skill is a directory plus a SKILL.md.
An 81-line dark theme (One-Dark-like) with named vars referenced by the colors map and an export palette for HTML output.
Five-line example prompt template with a description frontmatter; the body is a single instruction sentence.
Fifteen-line extension whose resources_discover hook returns the paths of its own SKILL.md, dynamic.md and dynamic.json, resolved from import.meta.url.
Registers echo_session at session_start and more tools from /add-echo-tool, validating names against /^[a-z0-9_]+$/ and carrying promptSnippet and promptGuidelines.
Persists a status card with appendEntry and renders it with registerEntryRenderer - durable extension data that appears in the transcript but not in the LLM context.
Inter-extension messaging via pi.events.on/emit with a namespaced event name, using a session_start-captured context for the notification.
Watches /tmp/agent-trigger.txt and injects its contents with pi.sendMessage({triggerTurn:true}), clearing the file after each read.
Creates a git stash create checkpoint per turn keyed by the leaf entry id and offers to stash apply it on session_before_fork; checkpoints are cleared on agent_settled.
Fetches and merges the upstream ref after each turn and, on conflict, sends the model a follow-up listing each conflict block with file, line range and ours/theirs sub-ranges.
#issue completion that preloads gh issues once per session and filters locally (numeric prefix first, then fuzzyFilter); first 90 of 185 lines read.
Single line node_modules/ for the Gondolin micro-VM example's dependency root.
Re-runs pi's built-in tools inside a Gondolin micro-VM by supplying pluggable Read/Write/Edit/Bash operations and translating host paths to the /workspace mount; first 120 of 531 lines read.

Generated npm lockfile (185 lines) for @earendil-works/gondolin 0.12.0 and its transitive tree; first 30 lines read to confirm the root and direct entries, but the remaining entries are the same machine-generated shape per package.
Manifest declaring pi.extensions and an exact-pinned dependency on @earendil-works/gondolin 0.12.0; tab-indented unlike the other example manifests.
/handoff command that summarises the branch into a self-contained prompt, offers it for editing and starts a NEW session with parentSession tracking, using the replacement context after the switch.
Minimal 26-line custom tool built with defineTool, returning content plus a details object.
Customises the collapsed thinking-block label via ctx.ui.setHiddenThinkingLabel, applied on session_start and resettable from a command.
Expands !{command} patterns inside a prompt through the input event, preserving whole-line ! commands, with a 30s per-command timeout and a reset of the module-level regex lastIndex.
39-line example of event.streamingBehavior === steer short-circuiting an expensive git diff --stat call so a correction reaches the model without delay.
Input-event example with the three outcomes (continue/transform/handled), a ?quick prefix transform, and instant non-LLM answers for ping and time.

user_bash hook that detects interactive commands (start-of-line or after the last pipe), stops the TUI and spawns them with stdio inherit; ~70-command allowlist plus INTERACTIVE_COMMANDS/EXCLUDE env overrides.
Virtual model that plans on Codex Sol/Terra (chosen by the Jev classifier) and switches once to Luna after the first successful edit, keeping the phase as branch-following router state.
Polls the macOS appearance with osascript every 2s and calls ctx.ui.setTheme on a change, clearing the interval on session_shutdown.
Registers a renderer for the status-update custom message type, colouring by level and showing a timestamp when expanded; the message participates in LLM context.
Re-registers all seven built-in tools with renderers that show only the call when collapsed and full output when expanded; first 80 of 353 lines read.
Vim-like modal editor extending CustomEditor, translating normal-mode keys into terminal escape sequences and falling through to the base for Escape and control keys.
model_select hook that shows provider/id in the status bar, notifies on change and stays silent when the source is a session restore.
Desktop notification on agent_settled (not agent_end) via OSC 777, OSC 99 or a Windows toast, selected from WT_SESSION/KITTY_WINDOW_ID.

1450-line manual QA suite exposing 13 slash commands that exercise overlay anchors, margins, stacking, overflow, animation, focus and streaming; first 60 lines read, the remaining 13 scenarios not read line by line.
Overlay with inline text inputs inside menu items, implementing Focusable with CURSOR_MARKER and renderFakeCursor; first 60 of 153 lines read.
34-line fail-closed safety gate on tool_call for rm -rf/sudo/chmod 777, blocking with {block:true,reason} when there is no UI to confirm in.
Toggles a pirate persona by appending to the system prompt in before_agent_start while still requiring the real task to be done correctly.
Plan-mode guide: the two-phase plan/execute model, the numbered Plan: output contract, the [DONE:n] marker protocol and the command allow/deny lists.

Plan mode: snapshots and restores the active tool set, allowlists bash, injects a display:false context message, filters that context back out when the mode is off, and rebuilds [DONE:n] progress from the branch after the last plan-mode-execute marker.
Pure testable helpers: isSafeCommand requires BOTH a non-matching destructive pattern and a matching safe pattern, plus the Plan: parser and the [DONE:n] marker applier.
Named presets (model/thinking/tools/instructions) merged from global and project presets.json, with the pre-preset state snapshotted so (none) can restore it exactly; first 309 of 436 lines read.
project_trust handler returning yes/no/undecided with an optional remember flag; the first handler that decides owns the prompt.
Adds a named system-prompt section derived from the ACTIVE tool set and skills, deleting the section when empty so the prompt cannot mention a disabled tool.
Blocks write/edit to .env, .git/ and node_modules/ via the tool_call hook, using a simple substring match on event.input.path.
18-line example logging the exact provider request payload and response headers via before_provider_request/after_provider_response, with a commented-out payload replacement.
/qna command that extracts questions from the last complete assistant message with a dedicated model and loads them into the editor; refuses incomplete messages.
Question tool with a full custom UI (options plus an inline Type-something editor), executionMode sequential, and a two-level escape ladder; first 80 of 286 lines read.
Multi-question variant of the question tool with a tab bar, machine value vs display label per option and a shared errorResult helper; first 80 of 448 lines read.
Custom editor that animates a shine highlight over the word ultrathink, starting and stopping a 60ms timer based on the editor text and post-processing the rendered lines.
Shows that ctx.reload() exists only on the command context: the tool queues /reload-runtime as a follow-up user message instead of reloading directly.
Exercises every RPC-supported ctx.ui method (select, confirm, input, editor, notify, setStatus, setWidget, setTitle, setEditorText) as a conformance harness for the extension-UI subprotocol.
Single line node_modules (no trailing slash, unlike the sibling examples).
OS-level bash sandboxing via @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime, with a merged sandbox.json (project over global) of network domain rules and filesystem deny/allow lists; first 120 of 321 lines read.

Generated npm lockfile (92 lines) for @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime 0.0.26 and its transitive tree; first 25 lines read to confirm the root and direct entries, the rest is the same machine-generated shape per package.
Manifest declaring pi.extensions and a dependency on @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime 0.0.26, the only example depending on an Anthropic-published package.
Four commands contrasting pi.sendUserMessage (a real user message) with pi.sendMessage, using ctx.isIdle to choose between a plain send, deliverAs steer and deliverAs followUp.
27-line command setting and reading the session display name via pi.setSessionName/getSessionName.
/quit plus two tools calling ctx.shutdown(), which requests a graceful shutdown deferred until the agent is idle so the tool result still reaches the model.
Snake game with a 100ms-tick TUI component and a high score kept outside the component for persistence; first 60 of 343 lines read.
Space-invaders game using the Kitty keyboard protocol for press/release detection, with aliens, bullets and destructible shields; first 60 of 560 lines read.

Delegates read/write/edit/bash to a remote host over SSH by supplying the tools' pluggable operations interfaces, base64-encoding writes and distinguishing abort from timeout; first 140 of 220 lines read.
32-line footer status showing turn progress through the keyed ctx.ui.setStatus API.
Tool returning terminate:true so the agent can end on the tool call without a follow-up turn, with the contract also stated to the model in promptGuidelines.

Subagent reference: the three modes and their limits, the security model (user-level agents by default, project agents need scope plus confirmation), the output display rules and the stated limitations.
Agent discovery from ~/.pi/agent/agents and the nearest .pi/agents above cwd, with a fail-soft frontmatter parser that accepts both YAML spellings of tools and never throws on one bad file.
Planning agent (read/grep/find/ls only) that emits a Goal/Plan/Files/Risks document written for a worker to execute verbatim.
Code-review agent that assumes tool permissions are not perfectly enforceable and keeps bash read-only, reporting Critical/Warnings/Suggestions with file:line references.
Recon agent returning compressed context (files with exact line ranges, key code, architecture) for a consumer that has not seen the files.
General-purpose agent with the default tool set, instructed to return Completed/Files Changed/Notes and a handoff checklist for the next agent.

1036-line subagent tool: spawns a separate pi process per task in single/parallel/chain mode, streams and parses the child's JSONL, aggregates usage, caps per-task output at 50KB and aborts with SIGTERM then SIGKILL.
Prompt template scripting a worker-reviewer-worker chain, passing each step's output to the next via the {previous} placeholder.
Prompt template scripting a scout-planner-worker chain with the {previous} placeholder and $@ argument.
Prompt template scripting a scout-planner chain that explicitly stops before implementation.
/summarize command that rebuilds a conversation transcript from the branch, summarises it with openai/gpt-5.2 and shows the result in a dismissible custom screen.
17-line example measuring the EFFECTIVE system prompt with ctx.getSystemPrompt() and showing its length in the status bar.

Game demonstrating executionMode sequential - sibling move_* calls race the final play under parallel execution - and keeping the user cursor out of the agent-visible details; first 70 of 1008 lines read.
Shows the two ways to bound a dialog - a timeout option on confirm/select and an explicit AbortController - and distinguishes a timeout from a user cancel.
Braille spinner in the terminal title driven by agent_start/agent_settled, with an idempotent stop that restores the base title.
Todo tool plus /todos command demonstrating branch-aware state stored in tool-result details and reconstructed by scanning the active branch on session_start and session_tree.
Overrides the built-in read tool with an audited version that blocks .env/secrets/.ssh/.aws paths, logs through withFileMutationQueue and keeps the built-in renderer.
/tools selector whose enabled set is persisted as a tools-config custom entry on the branch and restored (filtered to still-existing tools) on session_start and session_tree.
Edge-triggered compaction at 100k context tokens using ctx.getContextUsage and ctx.compact with onComplete/onError callbacks.
Reference truncation pattern: an rg wrapper using the package's own DEFAULT_MAX_LINES/DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES, truncateHead, a temp file for the full output and a notice stating what was omitted.
Nine-line example placing one widget above the editor and one below via ctx.ui.setWidget with the placement option.
Single line node_modules/ for the with-deps example's dependency root.
32-line tool that imports the third-party ms package, proving jiti resolves modules from the extension's own node_modules.
Generated npm lockfile (31 lines) for ms 2.1.3 and @types/ms 2.1.0; the whole file was read and is machine-generated dependency metadata with nothing to read line by line.
Manifest declaring pi.extensions, ms as a runtime dependency and @types/ms as a dev dependency - the smallest useful third-party dependency example.
Customises the streaming working indicator (dot/pulse/spinner/none/reset) via ctx.ui.setWorkingIndicator, with frames:[] as the hide mechanism and undefined as the reset.
17-line regression check that a custom working message and indicator set on session_start survive per-turn loader recreations.
35-line typed RPC client: starts the child, streams text deltas to stdout and tool banners to stderr, waits for settle via promptAndWait and stops cleanly.
Custom terminal chat client that speaks RPC and implements the extension-UI subprotocol (select/confirm/input/editor) using Pi's own TUI component kit; first 110 of 661 lines read.
Smallest SDK session: createAgentSession, subscribe to text deltas before prompting, print the messages and dispose in a finally.
Three ways to pick a model (getModel by provider/id, custom models from models.json, getAvailable which returns only credentialed models) plus the thinking level.
Replace the system prompt (also suppressing APPEND_SYSTEM.md) or append to it, both through DefaultResourceLoader overrides and in-memory sessions.
Discovers, filters and injects skills through skillsOverride, including a synthetic skill with a virtual path and sourceInfo.
Tool allowlists across built-in/extension/custom tools, and the rule that a custom cwd is applied when the built-in tools are built.
Loads extensions from additionalExtensionPaths and from inline factories, with a commented example extension showing agent_start, tool_call blocking and agent_end.
AGENTS.md discovery and injection through agentsFilesOverride, where an empty list disables context files entirely.
Adds a file-style prompt template through promptsOverride, with the synthetic sourceInfo helper shared with the skills example.
Three credential configurations: the default runtime, a runtime pointed at custom authPath/modelsPath files, and a per-provider runtime API key override.
Settings overrides with applyOverrides, the flush() durability boundary, drainErrors() for surfacing persistence failures, and an in-memory settings manager for tests.
Every session acquisition route - inMemory, create, continueRecent (which returns a modelFallbackMessage), list and open - plus a custom session directory.
Replaces every service, including a hand-written eleven-method ResourceLoader that asserts a fixed system prompt and no append sources.
Session replacement via createAgentSessionRuntime, with the bindSession() pattern that rebinds extensions and subscriptions after every newSession/switchSession.
Adds the codemode, tool_search and MCP extensions to an SDK session, enabling the first two through the +name defaultTools delta and calling bindExtensions to connect the MCP servers.
SDK example index, a quick-reference snippet and the createAgentSession option table with each default spelled out.
